statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-47300 (GHSA-8prm-248r-h957) is an elevation of privilege issue in the ASP.NET Core Negotiate authentication handler caused by improper validation, which affects applications that use Negotiate authentication with LDAP to retrieve role information. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate NuGet package as affected, 9.0.0 through 9.0.17 for .NET 9, fixed in 9.0.18 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8prm-248r-h957, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/409, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.18/9.0.18.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of these packages contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.dll or a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate nupkg. The Negotiate handler is distributed as a separate NuGet package and is not part of the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework that aspnetcore9-runtime and the SDK in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap carry, and the source-build nupkg set in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts does not include it. The same scan found the other ASP.NET Core assemblies by name (for example Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll at the build's version in every build), so the search itself works. An application that needs Negotiate authentication must add the package from NuGet itself, and is then covered by Microsoft's advisory for that package, not by this owner.
